 Possible tornadoes, damaging winds forecast for San Joaquin Valley on Thursday 
 by 
 Andrea Baltodano • Stocktonia 
 Nov. 18, 2026, 2:00 p.m. Nov. 18, 2026, 2:01 p.m.

 Parts of the San Joaquin Valley could see brief tornadoes Thursday afternoon as a storm system moves through Northern California, according to the National Weather Service.
 The agency’s Storm Prediction Center issued a severe weather outlook Wednesday, Nov. 18, identifying a marginal risk of severe thunderstorms across portions of the valley Thursday, Nov. 19.
 Forecasters said isolated thunderstorms could become strong enough to produce brief tornadoes and damaging wind gusts, particularly during the early to midafternoon.
 The Storm Prediction Center classified the threat as a marginal risk, the lowest of its five severe weather risk categories, meaning isolated severe thunderstorms are possible.
 As of Wednesday morning, the National Weather Service had not issued a tornado watch or warning for San Joaquin County.
 The potential for tornadoes comes as San Joaquin County faces heavy rainfall and strong winds associated with a storm system moving across the region.

 The National Weather Service in Sacramento said there is a 10% to 20% chance of thunderstorms Wednesday afternoon through early Thursday in the Sacramento-San Joaquin Delta and surrounding areas.
 Thunderstorm chances are expected to continue Thursday, when some storms could produce funnel clouds.
 Meanwhile, a wind advisory remains in effect through 10 p.m. Wednesday for Stockton, Lodi, Tracy and other parts of San Joaquin County.
 Southeast winds of 20 to 30 mph, with gusts reaching 55 mph, could knock down tree limbs, cause power outages and make driving difficult, particularly for high-profile vehicles.
 Forecasters expect rain to continue through Thursday, potentially causing localized flooding and hazardous road conditions.
 In Stockton, temperatures could reach the low 50s Wednesday and mid-50s Thursday. The weather should improve Friday before another round of rain arrives over the weekend..
 Residents can monitor the latest forecasts and weather alerts at weather.gov .
